title: Medical Content Producer
description: Job Title: Medical Content Producer Job Type: Full-Time / Remote Schedule: Monday–Friday Compensation: $565–$1,305/month USD (depending on experience) About the Role We are a US-based digital health media company producing daily medical news content across social media platforms. We are looking for a detail-oriented, highly organized Medical Content Producer to serve as the editorial backbone of our daily content operation. This person is responsible for finding, researching, and verifying the medical stories we cover each day, and transforming them into polished long-form scripts and carousel content that educates and engages our audience. This is a role for someone who genuinely loves medical news, takes accuracy seriously, and can work independently to meet daily production deadlines. Daily Responsibilities News Monitoring & Story Selection Monitor news aggregators, Google Alerts, Google News, and Feedly each morning for trending and breaking medical news Review primary sources including CDC, NIH, FDA, WHO, and peer-reviewed journals to identify and verify newsworthy stories Scan consumer-facing health news outlets including Stat News, MedPage Today, Medscape, and Medical News Today Select 5–7 of the most relevant, accurate, and audience-appropriate stories each day for content coverage Maintain a daily story tracker in Google Sheets or Notion documenting selected stories, sources, and key facts Long-Form Script Writing Write one fully researched, production-ready script per day for a 7–10 minute medical news roundup video show Scripts must be conversational, accurate, clearly sourced, and written for a general audience Scripts should include natural transitions between stories, a strong opening hook, and a clear closing Submit completed scripts by an agreed-upon daily deadline Carousel Content Creation Create one to two carousel posts per day (5–7 slides each) based on the day's selected stories Each carousel should include a strong headline slide, supporting information slides, and a call-to-action slide Write all carousel copy in clear, accessible language appropriate for social media audiences Lay out carousels in Canva or an equivalent tool, following brand guidelines provided Weekly Responsibilities Maintain and update a content calendar tracking all stories covered, scripts completed, and carousels produced Flag emerging health trends or recurring topics that could become series or recurring segments Participate in a weekly team check-in via Zoom or Google Meet You Are a Strong Fit If You: Have a background in health sciences, nursing, medicine, public health, journalism, or communications Write clean, accurate, conversational English at a native or near-native level Are comfortable reading and interpreting peer-reviewed medical research Can simplify complex medical findings for a general audience without sacrificing accuracy Are highly organized, self-directed, and able to meet firm daily deadlines Have strong attention to detail and take medical accuracy seriously Are familiar with US health media and current health topics Bonus Points For: Experience writing scripts for video content Familiarity with PubMed, NIH databases, or medical journals Experience using Canva for social media content creation Knowledge of health disparities, women's health, or minority women's health topics Experience with Notion, Google Workspace, Feedly, or similar tools To Apply, Please Submit: Your resume or CV Three writing samples — at least one must be health or medical related A short video introduction (2–3 minutes) telling us about yourself, your background, and your interest in health and medical content A brief writing test: Find a current medical news story, write a 200-word summary of it as if explaining it to a general audience, and list the primary sources you used to verify it

title: Implementation & Operations Specialist
description: About Pharmesol Pharmesol’s AI Pharmacy Assistant automates routine tasks and conversations so pharmacy teams can spend more time delivering exceptional patient care. We build pharmacy-specific AI systems that understand pharmacy workflows, medications, and patient interactions. Our technology is already live in pharmacies across the U.S., helping teams reduce operational burden while improving the patient experience. We are a fast-growing company operating at the intersection of healthcare and AI. The pace is high, the problems are complex, and the expectations are demanding. If you enjoy solving real operational problems and building systems that directly impact patient care, you will find this work deeply rewarding. About the Role We are looking for an Implementation Associate who will own the deployment of Pharmesol’s system with pharmacy customers. This is not a coordination or project management role. You will be responsible for figuring out how Pharmesol should actually work within each pharmacy’s operations. Every pharmacy operates differently. Departments change, workflows evolve, and edge cases appear constantly. Your job is to understand those details, design the correct workflow, and ensure the system behaves exactly as intended. You will work directly with pharmacy teams to map workflows, configure automation logic, test scenarios, and ensure a successful launch. At any given time you may be managing ~10 active implementations simultaneously, each with different operational nuances. The work requires exceptional attention to detail, strong reasoning ability, and the discipline to track many moving pieces without things slipping through the cracks. You will work closely with engineering, operations, and sales, but you own the implementation outcome end-to-end. Responsibilities Customer Implementation Lead implementation calls with pharmacy teams and operational stakeholders Deeply understand each pharmacy’s workflows, operational constraints, and edge cases Design how Pharmesol should integrate into those workflows Configure and test automation logic to ensure the system behaves correctly Identify missing information, inconsistencies, or operational risks during setup Run scenario testing to validate system behavior before launch Launch new customers and ensure the system performs as intended Operational Problem Solving Break down complex workflows into clear automation logic Anticipate edge cases and operational exceptions before they cause issues Diagnose problems quickly and determine whether the root cause is configuration, workflow, or system behavior Work closely with engineering when product changes are required Customer Ownership Maintain clear communication with pharmacy teams during implementation Ensure expectations are clear and timelines move forward In some cases, continue managing the account after launch or transition it to another tea ---------- mber About You This role is best suited for someone who naturally thinks in systems and details. Much of the job involves noticing inconsistencies, asking the right follow-up questions, and working through operational edge cases before they cause problems. You will likely do well in this role if the following feels natural to you: You notice inconsistencies quickly. When someone explains a workflow, you instinctively identify missing steps, unclear assumptions, or edge cases. You ask the right questions. You are comfortable probing until you fully understand how something actually works in practice. You can translate real-world processes into clear logic. You enjoy breaking down complex workflows into structured steps that can be implemented in a system. You stay organized across many parallel threads. You can manage ~10 implementations at once while keeping decisions, workflow logic, and next steps clearly documented. You take ownership for outcomes. If something is unclear or not working as expected, you investigate and resolve it rather than waiting for direction. You operate well in fast-moving environments. Priorities shift quickly, and you can context switch frequently without losing accuracy or attention to detail. This Role May Not Be a Good Fit If You struggle to context switch frequently. In this role, priorities shift often and you may move between multiple implementations throughout the day while still maintaining focus and accuracy. You are uncomfortable receiving direct, candid feedback. We value fast learning and open communication. Your default reaction when something goes wrong is to blame external factors or other people, rather than first asking what you could have done differently. You prefer environments where responsibilities are narrowly defined. This role requires high ownership and the ability to figure things out independently. Experience 2+ years of professional experience (excluding internships) Previous experience working in a fast-paced startup environment required Experience with U.S. healthcare operations strongly preferred Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience Technical / Operational Skills Strong analytical and problem-solving ability Comfortable learning new systems and workflows quickly Highly organized in tracking many concurrent details You have personally built or configured AI or automation workflows (not just used ChatGPT for writing). Hiring Process Because this role requires a high degree of ownership and independent thinking, our hiring process is rigorous. Final candidates should expect: Three reference calls, including at least two former direct managers Background check Why This Role Is Unique You will be working directly on the operational layer where AI meets real healthcare workflows. The problems are rarely obvious, the environments are constantly changing, and the solutions require both careful thinking and practical judgment. If you enjoy solving messy real-world problems and building systems that make frontline healthcare teams more effective, this role offers significant ownership and growth potential.

title: Claims Readiness Coordinator
description: Job Description: Claims Readiness Coordinator Department: Revenue Cycle Management / Billing Reports To: Billing Team / CEO Position Type: Full-Time Job Summary The Claims Readiness Coordinator serves as the essential gatekeeper of our billing pipeline. The primary mission of this role is to ensure all patient accounts and clinical documentation are audited, complete, and optimized "clean and fast" before being handed off to our Home Health Billers. By managing the pre-billing queue and proactively resolving documentation bottlenecks, you will directly accelerate our billing cycle, minimize claim denials, and protect the agency's cash flow. If you are a hyper-detailed organizer who loves solving puzzles, hunting down missing paperwork, and setting your team up for seamless financial success, this role is for you. Key Responsibilities • Pre-Billing Queue Management: Actively monitor, update, and manage the pre-billing list daily. Ensure all required compliance elements are met before claims are advanced to the billing stage. • Documentation Auditing & Quality Control: Review clinical documentation—including Physician Orders, History & Physicals (H&Ps), and face-to-face visit notes—for accuracy, signatures, and compliance to prevent future ADRs (Additional Documentation Requests) and denials. • Bottleneck Resolution: Proactively identify missing, saved or incomplete documentation. Collaborate directly with clinicians, nurses, and external provider offices to track down outstanding paperwork swiftly. • Payer-Specific Prep: Ensure all unique front-end requirements are met for various complex payers, including Managed Medicare, Commercial (primarily United and Blue Cross), and specialty accounts (Cook County, University of Chicago, Niko Health). • Biller Collaboration: Partner closely with the Home Health Billing team to pass off highly accurate, submission-ready claim data, acting as the first line of defense against rejections. • Process Optimization: Track common recurring errors or documentation delays and report trends to management to help improve front-end workflows. Qualifications & Skills • Experience: Minimum of 1–2 years of experience in healthcare administration, medical records, or a pre-billing/intake role (Home Health or DME experience is a major plus). • Knowledge: Basic understanding of medical terminology, insurance verification, and what constitutes a compliant clinical note or order. • Technical Savvy: Proficiency with Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems and billing platforms (experience with Niko Health or similar platforms is preferred). • The "Superpower" Traits: o Obsessive Attention to Detail: You catch the missing signature or incorrect date that everyone else misses. o Assertive Communication: You are comfortable but professional when nudging clinicians or external offices for delayed documentation. o Speed & Efficiency: You thrive in a fast-paced environment where keeping the pipeline moving is the top priority. What Success Looks Like in This Role • Clean Claim Rate: A dramatic reduction in front-end claim rejections because data is flawless before submission. • Days in AR reduction: Faster turnaround from patient visit to claim submission due to an optimized pre-billing list. • Seamless Teamwork: The Home Health Billers can focus entirely on clean submissions, appeals, and revenue recovery because the data arriving on their desks is pristine.

title: Lead Medical Biller & RCM
description: Job Description:  Lead Medical Biller & RCM Department: Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) Reports To: CEO Position Type: Full-Time Job Summary The Home Health & DME Billing Specialist is responsible for executing full-cycle billing operations across our Home Health, Durable Medical Equipment (DME), and Pharmacy business lines. This role balances standard commercial/government insurance collections with the strategic management of high-priority specialty accounts (including Cook County, University of Chicago, and Private Pay International patients). By implementing industry-standard billing protocols (PDGM, NOA, SWO) and aggressively managing accounts receivable, the Specialist ensures maximum, compliant reimbursement and resolves legacy outstanding revenue. Key Responsibilities 1. End-to-End Claim Management & Industry Protocols • Clean Claim Submission: Prepare, scrub, and submit clean claims daily. Manage electronic transmissions (837I/837P) and execute specialized paper claim submissions (UB-04 for Home Health; CMS-1500 for DME) to Managed Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payers. • Home Health Compliance: Adhere strictly to the Patient-Driven Groupings Model (PDGM) guidelines. Monitor the 5-day regulatory window for Notice of Admission (NOA) submissions to avoid late-filing payment penalties. Ensure accurate HIPPS coding mapping. • DME Compliance: Verify that all claims align with current CMS standard documentation requirements. Ensure a valid Standard Written Order (SWO) and Proof of Delivery (POD) are on file prior to billing. Stay updated on quarterly HCPCS Level II code and fee schedule modifications. 2. Denials, Appeals & ADR Management • Audit Response (ADR): Serve as the primary responder to Additional Documentation Requests (ADRs), with a heavy focus on UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross Blue Shield. Efficiently extract, compile, and audit clinical records (including Physician Orders, History & Physicals [H&Ps], and clinical visit notes) to fulfill audit deadlines. • Appeals & Rejections: Review, troubleshoot, and aggressively appeal rejected or denied claims. Correct front-end clearinghouse rejections and draft clinical appeal letters to secure maximum reimbursement. 3. Accounts Receivable (AR) & Payment Posting • AR Tracking & Collections: Maintain and manage the aging AR report. Routinely follow up on outstanding claims with payers to identify payment bottlenecks and prevent claims from exceeding Timely Filing Limits. • Payment Posting: Accurately post insurance reimbursements from Electronic Remittance Advices (ERAs/EOBs) and direct patient payments, keeping financial ledgers reconciled. 4. Prebilling & Workflow Synergy • Prebilling Optimization: Regularly update and audit the prebilling list. Collaborate with internal teams to ensure clinicians complete documentation in a timely manner, allowing claims to flow to the billing stage rapidly. Specialty Account Portfolios This position commands complete ownership over the following specialized and uninsured billing tracks: • Cook County (Uninsured Programs): Manage and bill dedicated tracks for Cook County, including DME, Pharmacy (utilizing the Niko Health platform), and Nursing/Palliative Home Health care. • Cook County Back-Billing: Lead revenue recovery efforts by analyzing, troubleshooting, and executing back-billing protocols for legacy, unpaid Cook County accounts. • University of Chicago (Uninsured DME): Process, bill, and monitor DME claims designated under the University of Chicago uninsured workflows. • International Patients (Private Pay DME): Coordinate specialized itemized billing, statement generation, and payment collections for international private pay accounts. Qualifications & Skills • Experience: 3+ years of medical billing experience, with specific exposure to Home Health (OASIS/PDGM workflows) and/or DME billing. • System Experience: Proficiency with electronic billing clearinghouses and EHRs. Direct experience with Niko Health is highly preferred. • Regulatory Knowledge: Deep understanding of CMS guidelines, UB-04 and CMS-1500 coding, prior authorization matrixes, and commercial insurance rules (particularly BCBS and UnitedHealthcare). • Core Competencies: Strong analytical skills for AR auditing, excellent communication skills for resolving complex payer issues, and a proactive mindset for hunting down older, unpaid cash flow. What Success Looks Like in This Role • First-Pass Clean Claim Rate: Maintaining an industry-standard first-pass claim acceptance rate of 95% or higher. • Days in AR: Significantly lowering the average Days in AR for the Cook County and University of Chicago portfolios. • Audit Resolution: 100% compliance and timely submission rates on all United and BCBS ADR packets, preventing clawbacks or unnecessary revenue loss.

description: About Health Shield Health Shield by Shiv Health is a mission-driven telehealth practice specializing in Chronic Care Management (CCM), Transitional Care Management (TCM), Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM), Remote Therapeutic Monitoring (RTM), and Behavioral Health Integration (BHI) services. We focus on improving outcomes for vulnerable and senior populations across Pennsylvania through proactive, technology-enabled care coordination. Our team helps patients with complex chronic conditions stay healthier at home while supporting compliant, high-quality billing and documentation. Position Summary We are seeking a proactive, organized, and clinically experienced Virtual Medical Assistant who will function as a Virtual Practice Manager. This is an elevated role that combines traditional medical assistant duties with significant practice management and care coordination responsibilities. You will serve as a central hub for prior authorizations, insurance eligibility, multi-provider care coordination, and remote monitoring oversight. Care coordination is the core of this position — you will frequently make phone calls to clinics, labs, and imaging centers to ensure patients receive timely services. You will also monitor RPM dashboards, review vitals and device data transmission, and help keep our chronic care programs running smoothly and compliantly. This is a phone-based role (no video required for patient or provider interactions). Strong English fluency and professional phone presence are essential. Key Responsibilities Prior Authorizations & Insurance Workflows •  Complete prior authorizations for medications, procedures, DME, and other services. •  Perform insurance eligibility verification and benefits checks for new and existing patients. Care Coordination (Primary Focus) •  Proactively schedule labs, diagnostic imaging, specialist appointments, follow-up visits, and other ancillary services. •  Make professional outbound and inbound phone calls to external clinics, labs, imaging centers, and providers to coordinate care and close gaps. •  Track and manage care gaps across patient panels to support timely interventions. Remote Patient Monitoring & Dashboard Oversight •  Log into RPM dashboards to review vital signs and device data transmission (blood pressure, glucose, weight, SpO2, etc.). •  Identify missing data, alerts, or transmission issues and escalate appropriately to the clinical team. •  Support accurate documentation and time tracking for CCM, TCM, RTM, and BHI billing compliance. You will help document: - Chief complaint - History of present illness - Past medical history - Past surgical history - Medication reconciliation - Allergies - Social history when relevant - Review of systems when relevant - Physical exam findings - Imaging and diagnostic history - Prior treatment history - Assessment / medical diagnoses - Treatment plan - Medication plan - Procedure plan - Follow-up plan - Medical necessity support You must be able to listen carefully, understand clinical information, and turn the encounter into a clean note that the physician can quickly review, edit, and sign. -------------------------------------------------- WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR -------------------------------------------------- The ideal candidate may have a background as a: - Experienced medical scribe - Registered Nurse - Physical Therapist - Pharmacist - Physician / medical graduate - Medical Technologist - Healthcare BPO professional with clinical documentation experience - Medical transcriptionist with live scribing experience - Clinical documentation specialist A license is not strictly required. You should be comfortable documenting relevant history related to: - Depression - Anxiety - PTSD - Sleep problems - Mood symptoms - Functional impairment - Medication history - Treatment response - Safety concerns when discussed by the provider You are not making psychiatric decisions. You are documenting accurately under physician direction. -------------------------------------------------- WORKERS' COMPENSATION / IME EXPERIENCE -------------------------------------------------- Workers' Compensation or Independent Medical Evaluation experience is strongly preferred. Helpful experience includes documenting or summarizing: - Date of injury - Mechanism of injury - Work status - Job duties - Restrictions - Prior treatment chronology - Imaging history - Procedure history - Medication history - Functional limitations - MMI-related information - Impairment-related information - Causation-related history - Record review summaries - Contradictions or missing records You are not expected to make legal or medical conclusions. Paid time must be focused only on our credentialing work. -------------------------------------------------- REQUIRED EXPERIENCE ------------------------------------------ ---------- to 5 years of US healthcare credentialing or provider enrollment experience - Hands-on CAQH experience - Hands-on PECOS / Medicare provider enrollment experience - NPPES / NPI update experience - Commercial payer enrollment experience - Experience submitting and tracking payer applications - Experience following up with payers by portal, email , and phone - Experience maintaining credentialing trackers or spreadsheets - Strong written English - Strong attention to detail - Ability to work independently - High confidentiality and professionalism -------------------------------------------------- STRONGLY PREFERRED EXPERIENCE -------------------------------------------------- - Physician practice credentialing - Specialty clinic credentialing - Pain management, anesthesia, orthopedic, spine, PM&R, neurology, ASC, or procedural-specialty experience - Hospital or surgery center privileging - Medicare and Medicaid enrollment - Commercial payer enrollment with BCBS, UHC/Optum, Aetna, Cigna, Humana, and regional payers - EFT / ERA / EDI enrollment - Payer contracting support - Recredentialing and revalidation - Workers' Compensation network enrollment - Experience handling sensitive provider disclosures, malpractice history, training gaps, licensure questions, or application explanations - CPES, CPCS, CPMSM, CPB, CPC, or other healthcare credentialing/billing certification Certifications are preferred but not required. Real hands-on credentialing experience matters more than certificates. -------------------------------------------------- MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES -------------------------------------------------- You may be responsible for: - Maintaining CAQH profile - Uploading and updating CAQH documents - CAQH attestations / re-attestations - Authorizing payer access in CAQH - Maintaining PECOS / Medicare enrollment information - Tracking Medicare revalidations - Maintaining NPPES / NPI information - Updating taxonomy, address, contact, and practice information - Submitting commercial payer enrollment applications - Tracking payer application status - Following up with payers until approval - Confirming payer effective dates - Supporting payer contracting paperwork - Supporting EFT / ERA / EDI setup - Helping connect payer approvals to billing/clearinghouse workflow - Tracking payer portal logins and status updates - Maintaining a credentialing tracker - Maintaining a license / DEA / CME / malpractice renewal calendar - Assisting with hospital and surgery center privilege applications - Tracking hospital reappointment deadlines - Organizing peer references and privilege documents - Organizing malpractice insurance certificates and loss runs - Organizing board certification, CME, ACLS/BLS, and other documents - Organizing sensitive disclosure documents for provider review - Preparing weekly or monthly status reports -------------------------------------------------- CONFIDENTIALITY REQUIREMENT -------------------------------------------------- This role involves sensitive physician credentialing information. You may see private information related to medical licenses, malpractice history, training history, insurance applications, hospital privileges, DEA registration, government portals, and payer applications. You must be extremely confidential. You may not: - Share clinic or provider information - Save documents to your personal computer - Upload documents to your personal Google Drive, Dropbox, or email - Forward clinic documents to outside accounts - Upload clinic documents into ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or any outside AI tool without written approval - Share logins - Subcontract the work - Allow another person to access our documents or portals A confidentiality agreement and HIPAA/BAA may be required before access is granted. -------------------------------------------------- SENSITIVE DISCLOSURE RULE -------------------------------------------------- Some credentialing applications ask sensitive yes/no questions about malpractice claims, training history, licensure history, hospital privileges, investigations, or professional issues. You are not expected to make legal or professional judgment calls. Your responsibility is to: - Flag every sensitive disclosure question - Organize the requested information - Draft a clear factual summary if asked - Send the question and draft to the physician for review - Wait for physician approval before submission - Never guess - Never hide information - Never answer a sensitive question without approval - Never submit an application with incomplete or inaccurate disclosure information Accuracy, honesty, and confidentiality are mandatory. -------------------------------------------------- TRACKING AND REPORTING -------------------------------------------------- Every application or follow-up must be documented. Your credentialing tracker should include: - Payer or facility name - Portal used - Application type - Date started - Date submitted - Confirmation number - Reference number - Contact person - Current status - Missing items - Next follow-up date - Approval date - Effective date - EFT / ERA / EDI status if applicable - Notes and blockers A short weekly status report will be required. Weekly report should include: - Applications submitted - Applications pending - Payers or facilities contacted - Reference numbers obtained - Missing documents needed from physician - Sensitive disclosure questions needing physician review - Renewals coming due - Problems or delays - Next week priorities -------------------------------------------------- WORK STYLE -------------------------------------------------- This is a part-time role, but paid time must be focused on our work. During paid working time: - You must work only on our credentialing tasks - You may not bill time while working for another client - You may not subcontract the work - You must document actual work completed - You must update the credentialing tracker - You must be available for scheduled check-ins - You must be able to explain what you completed This role is best for someone who is organized, detail-oriented, experienced, confidential, and able to work independently. -------------------------------------------------- DO NOT APPLY IF -------------------------------------------------- Please do not apply if: - You have no US healthcare credentialing experience - You have never used CAQH - You have never used PECOS - You do not understand provider enrollment - You only know insurance verification - You only know medical billing but not credentialing - You cannot maintain a detailed tracker - You are not comfortable with sensitive confidential information - You need to be trained from the beginning - You cannot follow up with payers consistently - You cannot work independently - You plan to subcontract this role - You are not willing to complete a live screen-share skills test -------------------------------------------------- SELECTION PROCESS -------------------------------------------------- Qualified applicants may be asked to complete: - Written screening questions - Short video interview - Live screen-share workflow test - Credentialing tracker review - Paid trial task - 30-day probationary period We are not hiring based on interview confidence. We are hiring based on demonstrated credentialing skill, organization, confidentiality, and follow-through. -------------------------------------------------- HOW TO APPLY -------------------------------------------------- Your application will only be considered if you follow these instructions. The first line of your application must be: CREDENTIALING EXPERT - CAQH PECOS Then answer these questions: 1. How many years of US healthcare credentialing or provider enrollment experience do you have? 2. Have you personally worked in CAQH? Describe exactly what tasks you performed. 3. Have you personally worked in PECOS? Describe exactly what tasks you performed. 4. Have you personally updated NPPES / NPI information? What types of updates have you done? 5. Which commercial payers have you credentialed providers with? Examples: BCBS, UHC/Optum, Aetna, Cigna, Humana, Medicare Advantage plans, Medicaid plans, regional payers. 6. Have you handled hospital or surgery center privilege applications? If yes, describe your experience. 7. Have you handled Medicare revalidation, Medicaid enrollment, or payer recredentialing? Give examples. 8. Have you handled EFT / ERA / EDI enrollment after payer approval? Explain your workflow. 9. What credentialing tracker or spreadsheet have you used? Describe the columns you would include. 10. Describe a time when a payer application was stuck, returned incomplete, or delayed. What did you do to fix it? 11. Have you ever handled sensitive provider disclosures such as malpractice history, training gaps, licensure questions, or disciplinary questions? How did you handle confidentiality and provider approval? 12. What certifications do you have, if any? Examples: CPES, CPCS, CPMSM, CPB, CPC, healthcare administration, medical billing, credentialing training. 13. Are you currently working for other clients? If yes, list your current schedule and confirm that you will not bill us while working for another client. 14. What is your requested hourly rate in USD? 15. Are you available for a live screen-share test where you walk through a sample CAQH / PECOS / payer enrollment workflow? -------------------------------------------------- MINI TEST QUESTION -------------------------------------------------- A solo physician is already in-network with some payers, but the CAQH profile, NPPES profile, malpractice certificate, DEA certificate, and payer enrollment tracker may be outdated. Walk me through exactly how you would audit and clean up the credentialing file during the first 30 days. Your answer should mention CAQH, PECOS, NPPES, payer applications, commercial payers, Medicare, DEA, state license, malpractice insurance, hospital privileges, EFT / ERA / EDI, credentialing tracker, missing documents, and follow-up schedule.

title: Quality Assurance Nurse
description: Job Title: Clinical Quality Assurance Nurse – UK Care Home Group (Remote) Job Type: Full-Time | Work From Home | UK Hours About Us We are a UK-based group of nine care homes providing residential and nursing care across England. We are regulated by the Care Quality Commission (CQC) and operate to high standards of clinical governance. As part of our quality assurance framework we are building a dedicated remote QA function to provide independent oversight of care quality and compliance across all our homes. This Is Not a Standard Remote Nursing Role We are not looking for someone to answer calls, manage schedules, or provide telehealth support. This role requires a nurse who can open a care record and tell whether the care being delivered is genuinely good — not just whether the paperwork is present. You will be reviewing real care records for real residents and your findings will directly influence the quality of care they receive. This is serious clinical governance work and we need someone who takes that responsibility seriously. What You Will Do Each day you will be assigned one of our nine care homes to audit remotely. You will have direct access to our care management system (Person Centred Software) and our audit platform (Go Audits) and will work through a structured audit tool covering: Reviewing every audit the home manager has completed — not just whether they exist but whether they are meaningful, accurate, and followed up Checking every active Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) authorisation for that home — expiry dates, conditions, and whether applications are in place where needed Reviewing every i ---------- and a ---------- logged since your last visit — completeness, post-fall observations, patterns, escalation, and CQC notifications Deep clinical review of 3 residents per visit: Full care plan assessment — is it person-centred, current, and does it reflect this individual's actual needs or is it generic and copy-pasted? All risk assessments — falls, pressure care, nutrition, mental capacity, moving and handling, continence, oral health, skin integrity, communication needs MAR chart audit — gaps, PRN protocols, controlled drug records, time-sensitive medications, topical charts Nutrition and weight monitoring — MUST scores, weight trends, dietician referrals, supplement prescriptions, texture-modified diets Pressure care — Waterlow scores, repositioning charts, wound care plans, body maps, escalation End of life care planning where applicable GP and allied health professional involvement and follow-through Continence and catheter care Behaviours that challenge — PBS plans, restrictive practice recording Home-level checks each visit: Staffing and mandatory training compliance Infection prevention and control Health and safety — fire drills, Legionella, COSHH Complaints and compliments Resident and family voice Handover record quality At the end of each day you will produce a written findings report with a RAG rating for the home, flagging any concerns to the UK clinical lead for follow-up. What We Are Looking For Essential: Registered Nurse with a minimum of 3 years post-qualification experience Experience in audit, quality assurance, compliance review, or clinical governance — in any country or healthcare setting Ability to read a care record and assess whether the care is genuinely good — not just whether the documentation is present Excellent written English — your reports will be read by UK registered managers and senior management Strong attention to detail and the ability to work independently and manage your own time Reliable internet connection and a quiet, professional working environment Willingness to learn UK care home regulatory standards Highly Desirable: Experience working in a long-term care, hospice, palliative care, or geriatric setting Experience with EMR or care management systems — any platform Previous QA, audit, or inspection preparation experience Experience reviewing medication records or MAR charts Any exposure to UK healthcare — NHS, UK care home work, or supporting UK-based clinical teams remotely Working Hours Our Hours will be: 8:30AM - 5:30PM UK (40 hours) (60 min lunch break) Philippines Timing: 3:30PM - 12:30AM Monday - Friday Total 40 hours per week

description: Private Online Psychiatric Mental Health Tutor (Doctor or equivalent) Nonprofit Educational Initiative About This Opportunity This opportunity is part of a nonprofit educational mission focused on supporting learning and development in the field of mental health. The goal is to help equip individuals with strong foundational knowledge in psychiatric mental health, especially for future service, education, and mission driven work. By participating, you will be contributing to a meaningful initiative that aims to expand understanding and access to mental health education. Role Overview We are looking for a licensed doctor, preferably a psychiatrist, or another highly qualified licensed mental health professional based in the Philippines to provide private one on one online tutoring in psychiatric mental health. This is a paid education project. It is not a clinical role, not for patient care, not for independent practice, and not a substitute for formal school, certification, or licensure. The purpose of this role is to deliver structured, high quality education in the core areas of psychiatric mental health knowledge. About the Student The student has a healthcare background, strong CDI and clinical documentation experience, and a strong ability to learn quickly. She already understands medical documentation and clinical workflows, but now wants to build deeper knowledge in psychiatric mental health. She works full time, so the program must be: • practical • organized • efficient • flexible What We Are Looking For We are not looking for casual tutoring. We are looking for someone who can: • mentor and guide the student in a structured way • design a clear learning pathway from start to finish • build a condensed, goal oriented program • help bridge clinical documentation knowledge into psychiatric thinking Your role is to equip and develop the student’s understanding in a serious and structured way, similar to a mentor or preceptor style relationship, but strictly for education only. You should be able to take someone with a strong documentation background and help her understand how mental health professionals: • assess patients • think through symptoms • form diagnoses • choose treatment approaches • understand medication logic • document psychiatric encounters • plan ongoing care Program Expectations The program should be structured and intentional, not random sessions. We are especially interested in applicants who can propose a clear and realistic learning plan explaining: • how you would take the student from point A to point Z • how you would structure the learning, such as weekly sessions, modules, exercises, or guided case discussions • how you would pace the program for someone working full time • what outcomes the student should achieve by the end We expect approximately one session per week, although you may recommend the structure you believe is best. Ideally, we hope the program can be taught in a boot camp style format, with the goal of bringing the student to a strong crash course level of psychiatric mental health knowledge in about 12 weeks or less, if realistic. We are open to your professional judgment on how best to structure this. Core Topics to Cover The program should build strong knowledge in areas such as: • psychiatric assessment • psychiatric interviewing • mental status examination • DSM based diagnosis • differential diagnosis • psychopharmacology • medication selection and reasoning for learning purposes only • treatment planning • care planning • psychiatric documentation, including SOAP style notes • case based discussion • clinical reasoning • safety and risk assessment • crisis awareness and escalation thinking • basic psychotherapy concepts • patient education • follow up thinking and longitudinal care planning We are also especially interested in candidates who can teach the core foundation often associated with advanced psychiatric training, including the 3 Ps: • advanced pathophysiology • advanced pharmacology • advanced health assessment The overall goal is to help the student build the type of psychiatric mental health knowledge commonly developed in PMHNP style training, while fully understanding that this tutoring program is for education only. End Goal By the end of the program, the student should have a strong educational foundation in how psychiatric mental health professionals think and approach: • assessment • diagnosis • treatment options • medication reasoning • documentation • care planning This is about developing clinical thinking and understanding, not simply memorizing information. Important Clarification This program is strictly for education and knowledge building only. It does not replace formal PMHNP education, certification, or licensure. The student is not seeking to practice based on this program alone. Who This Is Best For We are looking for: • licensed doctor preferred • psychiatrist strongly preferred • other licensed mental health professionals with strong psychiatric experience may be considered Ideal candidates will be: • experienced in psychiatric or mental health care • able to teach clearly in English • comfortable with one on one online teaching • organized, reliable, and professional • experienced in teaching, mentoring, tutoring, precepting, or curriculum building • able to design a structured learning program A practicing doctor in the Philippines who wants flexible remote teaching work may be a strong fit. Program Setup • fully remote and online • private one on one format • flexible schedule • approximately one session per week, or as proposed • short term, structured program preferred • Zoom based sessions are acceptable Budget • total budget: PHP 35,000 for the full program Application Requirements To apply, please send to: ---------- • your CV or resume • your professional background • your license and credentials • your psychiatric or mental health experience • any teaching, tutoring, mentoring, or precepting experience • a short introduction video of 3 minutes or less introducing yourself, your experience, and your teaching style • a brief proposal explaining: ?• how you would structure the program ?• how you would take the student from a clinical documentation background to strong psychiatric mental health knowledge ?• what your teaching approach would be ?• what outcomes you expect by the end • your availability for an interview Final Note This is a unique opportunity to combine professional expertise with meaningful educational impact. As part of this nonprofit initiative, your contribution helps support mental health education and future service in this field. We are looking for someone who takes teaching seriously and is willing to guide the student with clarity, structure, and purpose.

Performance is judged by: - Accurate billing work - Claims moved forward - Denials resolved - Payments posted correctly - Clear claim notes - Timely follow-up - Good communication - Ability to work independently Paid time must match real billing work and documented output. -------------------------------------------------- COMMUNICATION EXPECTATIONS -------------------------------------------------- You must be available during US Central business hours. If you are on a payer call, in a meeting, or working on a focused task, that is understandable. title: Virtual Medical Scheduler
description: VISTA DERMATOLOGY Virtual Medical Scheduler Remote · Full-Time ABOUT VISTA DERMATOLOGY Vista Dermatology is an independent, physician-owned private practice built on a simple but powerful belief: every patient deserves to be treated like family. Unlike large corporate dermatology groups, every person on our schedule is fully ours, and we take that responsibility seriously. Our patient experience begins the ---------- nt someone picks up the phone or submits an online request. We’ve built a reputation for excellence in clinical care, and we protect that reputation just as fiercely in every scheduling interaction. Our staff isn’t just answering a phone line, they’re nurturing relationships and setting the tone for everything that follows. We’re a small but fast-growing practice. In our first year, we went from a team of eight to fourteen, and we’re continuing to grow. We compensate our team competitively, invest in their development, and have a strong track record of long-term retention. Our tea ---------- mbers stay—and we’re proud of that. ROLE OVERVIEW We’re hiring our first Virtual Medical Scheduler: a remote, full-time hire who will serve as the first voice our patients hear. This is a high-volume, detail-critical scheduling role supporting a dermatology practice that handles 400–500 incoming calls per week across our appointment lines. This isn’t a vague support role. It’s a focused, essential function: answer calls, schedule patients accurately, enter the right insurance information into our practice management system, and represent Vista Dermatology with warmth and professionalism on every single interaction. If we hire well, we intend to hire a second virtual scheduler shortly after, and we’re committed to making this a stable, long-term position with a clear compensation path and real professional investment over time. SCHEDULE & AVAILABILITY This role requires consistent, predictable availability. Our phones open at a set time each morning, and our patients expect someone to be there. - Hours: 7:45 AM – 4:15 PM, Monday through Friday (40 hours/week) - Time Zone: Central Time (US) - Lunch break: 12:15 PM – 12:45 PM (30 minutes) - The 7:45 AM start allows time to review email s, check messages, and be ready before calls begin - Phones close to active callers at 4:00 PM; the final 15 minutes are used to close out to-do lists and contact the manager with any remaining questions - Attendance is non-negotiable — this is the first point of contact for our patients - Tardiness policy: notify the office manager by phone at least 10 minutes before your start time if late; no more than 2 late arrivals per rolling 30-day period - Punctuality is treated as a core professional standard, not a preference WHAT YOU'LL DO Your day will be primarily driven by live call volume, with additional responsibilities added incrementally as you become proficient. Tasks are prioritized in the following order: 1. Live Scheduling Calls (Primary Responsibility) - Answer 200–300+ inbound scheduling calls per week with professionalism and warmth - Collect accurate patient demographic, insurance, and appointment information - Enter all information correctly into our EMA (Modernizing Medicine/ModMed) practice management system; this is the first entry point of the patient chart - Verify insurance eligibility using our credentialing grid (updated regularly; the most current version must always be used) - Send patients the correct intake paperwork and obtain required credit card authorizations - Follow each scheduling step consistently and in order — every time, without skipping steps - Transfer calls appropriately when a patient has a clinical question outside the scope of scheduling 2. Online Scheduling Support (Added After Proficiency) - Process online scheduling requests and messages submitted through the patient portal - Manage online scheduling queue after demonstrating consistency on live calls 3. Voi cemail & Reschedule Callbacks (Added After Proficiency) - Return voi cemail messages within a strict callback window - Handle reschedule requests and cancellations professionally 4. Fax & Referral Processing (Added After Proficiency) - Process incoming fax referrals and scheduling records from outside providers WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR This role is not high-level complexity, but it demands a very specific kind of person. The work that looks deceptively simple on paper consistently separates strong performers from those who don’t make it past week two. You're a fit if you: - Have excellent spoken and written English — clarity and professionalism are non-negotiable - Type 50–70 words per minute with high accuracy - Are calm, patient, and consistent even during high call volume - Are naturally detail-oriented and take following a process seriously - Can sit at a computer for extended periods and navigate modern software with ease - Value stability and doing one thing excellently - Have a computer-comfortable background: past work in data entry, sales systems, student platforms, or similar computer-heavy environments - Understand that accuracy matters more than speed in the early stages - Are comfortable working during U.S. Central Time business hours This Role Is NOT a Fit If You: - Thrive on constant variety and creative problem-solving - Prefer physical, hands-on work environments - Have difficulty sitting attentively at a computer for a full workday - Are looking for a steppingstone to a different kind of role quickly - Are not comfortable with detailed, step-by-step processes that must be followed precisely - Have limited experience with modern computer systems or software TOOLS & SYSTEMS YOU'LL WORK WITH You do not need prior experience with these specific platforms, but you must be comfortable and confident with modern computer systems. Our staff has consistently found that tech-savvy individuals pick up our systems quickly. - ModMed (EMA / Modernizing Medicine): our all-in-one electronic health record, scheduling, and practice management system - Klara: HIPAA-compliant secure messaging with patients - RingCentral: our phone system (call volume is monitored and reviewed weekly) - Gusto: payroll and time tracking - Insurance Credentialing Grid: must be reviewed and used on every scheduling call; updated regularly - HIPAA compliance is expected in all digital communications: all patient information is protected health information (PHI) TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Because this is a remote, HIPAA-regulated role, your home setup must meet the following minimum standards before your start date: Internet & Connectivity - Minimum 10 Mbps download / 5 Mbps upload speeds (25 Mbps preferred for video) - A direct Ethernet (LAN) cable connection is strongly preferred over Wi-Fi for maximum stability - A backup internet source is required Hardware & Software - PC with at least Intel Core i5 or AMD Ryzen 5 processor and 8 GB RAM (16 GB preferred) - Operating system: Windows 10/11 or macOS 12+ - HD webcam (minimum 720p) for video check-ins - High-quality noise-canceling headset — critical for clear communication and patient privacy - A secure, enterprise-grade VPN and antivirus software to meet HIPAA requirements - Familiarity with cloud-based infrastructure (our EHR is fully cloud-based) - Familiarity with HIPAA-compliant communication platforms (e.g., Zoom for Healthcare, Microsoft Teams, Slack) Environment - Quiet, distraction-free workspace - Secure physical environment appropriate for handling protected health information (PHI) TRAINING & ONBOARDING We take onboarding seriously. We’ve grown quickly and trained several rounds of employees, and we’ve developed a structured onboarding approach that sets people up for success. We’ll apply a similar approach for our first virtual hire. - Week 1: Observational training — watching and learning alongside an experienced tea ---------- mber; ModMed video tutorials; meeting with office manager at end of week - Week 2: Graduated training — practicing scheduling with live supervision; check-in with office manager at end of week - Weeks 3–12: Increasing independence on calls; weekly touchpoints and performance reviews throughout - Day 90: Formal performance review with the office manager Our experience is consistent: those who adapt to the system do so quickly. Those who don’t fit the role make that clear in the first one to two weeks. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS We believe the best way to reward great work is through a strong, reliable hourly rate with clear raises you can count on as you grow with us. We’ll define a formal title progression (Scheduler I, Scheduler II, Scheduler III) tied to tenure, performance metrics, and peer feedback, so you’re always advancing—even when the work itself stays consistent. Months 1–3 (Onboarding): $6.00/hour Months 4–6: $6.50/hour Months 7–12: $7.00/hour Year 2: $7.50–$8.00/hour (based on performance review) Year 3+: $8.50+/hour (based on performance review) Every step up is tied to performance. Show up consistently, handle calls with care, and follow the process, and the raises will follow. We want you to see exactly what you’re working toward. Additional Benefits - 13th Month Bonus: One additional month’s salary paid at year-end (a standard Philippine benefit we are proud to honor) - Annual healthcare allowance: $432/year - Performance bonuses tied to call volume and quality metrics - Equipment & connectivity stipend: available after 12 months of strong performance (a reward for loyalty and consistency, not a day-one entitlement) - Payroll processed twice monthly via Gusto Time Off Full-time employees (30+ hours/week) earn paid time off based on hours worked: - Years 1–2: PTO accrues at 3.08 hours per 80 hours worked (10 days/year) - Years 2–4: PTO accrues at 4.61 hours per 80 hours worked (15 days/year) - Year 5+: PTO accrues at 5.84 hours per 80 hours worked (19 days/year) In addition, 6 paid U.S. holidays are observed each year: New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. Combined with PTO, total paid days off are 16 per year (years 1–2), 21 per year (years 2–4), and 25 per year (year 5+). - PTO begins accruing on your start date but may not be used until after the 180-day probationary period - PTO must be requested at least 4 weeks in advance (28 days); sick leave follows a separate process COMMUNICATION & SUPERVISION We use a structured, transparent management approach. You will never feel like you’re working alone without direction or feedback. - Weekly check-ins with the office manager throughout your first 90 days - Formal semi-annual performance reviews - For urgent scheduling questions during your shift: contact the supervising Medical Assistant via RingCentral - For non-urgent issues: email the office manager at any time - For face-to-face conversations or screen sharing: Google Meet - Performance tracked weekly via RingCentral (call volume) and ModMed (scheduling activity) We are an approachable team. We’d rather you ask a question than handle something incorrectly, especially when it comes to insurance data and patient communication. When in doubt, ask. Always. WHY THIS ROLE MIGHT BE PERFECT FOR YOU You’re not just filling a seat, you are Vista Dermatology’s first impression. You’re the voice our patients hear before they ever meet a physician or step into a treatment room. That means something. If you’re someone who finds deep satisfaction in doing one thing really well, in being the dependable constant in a busy medical practice, and in knowing that your work directly contributes to patient care—this role was made for you. We offer stability, growth, real professional investment, and a team that will treat you as a valued member, not a remote resource. We’re looking for someone who wants to stay, to grow within this role, and to be part of building something lasting. To Apply, please click the following link - ---------- Here, you will be prompted to upload a resume, fill out an Experience Questionnaire and take a quick assessment. If you pass this first round, we will send you a few follow up assessments. The last round will involve sending in a video recording of yourself answering a handful of questions, then finally a live face-to-face interview. Then we will make our final decision. Please Note: It is best to have already taken your English Proficiency Assessment on your Onlinejobs.ph profile through ---------- and the IQ Test through ---------- before applying since we will request both of these in the application process. It is not mandatory to have them completed but it will improve your chances of moving along in the process. We’re excited to find the right person — and when we do, we intend to invest in them for the long haul. — The Vista Dermatology Team

This role supports U.S. Eastern Time (ET) business hours. Because the Philippines is roughly 12–13 hours ahead of ET, scheduled shifts fall overnight in Philippine local time; the legally required night-shift differential applies to hours worked between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM Philippine time. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES • Place outbound, post-discharge calls to patients recently discharged from NYC Health + Hospitals facilities (Bellevue, Elmhurst, Kings County, Lincoln, Metropolitan, and Woodhull), following Colure Health’s Care Continuity Outreach Playbook call flow: Verify – Safety – Reason – Path – Barrier – Close – Document. • Verify patient identity (name and date of birth) and confirm permission before discussing care details with a caregiver or family member. • Run the safety screen on every call to surface emergency or same-day clinical issues before scheduling; immediately direct patients to 911 or 988 and stop routine scheduling when a red-flag symptom is reported. • Determine the correct follow-up pathway — PCP, specialist, telehealth fast-track, or same-day clinical escalation — and close every reachable, safe call with a booked appointment as the primary outcome. • Identify and resolve real-time barriers to care (transportation, language, childcare, work conflicts, cost concerns, distrust) using the zero-barrier approach; no referral form or insurance question is used as a reason to delay scheduling. • Offer immediate PCP assignment to patients who do not have, or have lost contact with, a primary care provider. • Apply the Acknowledge – Reframe – Solve – Close objection-handling framework to move hesitant patients toward a scheduled next step. • Receive each patient after an Enrollment Specialist has already reviewed the provider/discharge list, verified eligibility and insurance, obtained consent, and set the patient up in Mozaiq Care+ — using that completed intake to move straight into the safety screen and scheduling conversation instead of re-collecting information. • Document every call outcome in Mozaiq Care+ using the required outcome code (appointment booked, next step assigned, unable to reach, refused, same-day escalation, or emergency escalation) along with barrier, urgency, owner, deadline, permission status, and next action. • Adapt scripts for elderly, limited-English-proficiency, behavioral-health, and caregiver-involved patients, and for those enrolled in MLTC, FIDA, or PACE plans, using qualified interpreter support where needed. • Meet quality and productivity standards measured against the Manager QA Scorecard (opening and trust, privacy and permission, safety screen, pathway accuracy, barrier resolution, conversion close, documentation, and role boundaries). REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS • Excellent spoken and written English (C1 / near-native); Tagalog or another Philippine language is a plus but not required, since calls are conducted in English. • High school diploma or equivalent; coursework or experience in healthcare, customer service, or call-center operations is a plus. • 6+ months of experience in a contact-center, customer-service, healthcare-support, or patient-facing role. • Comfortable following a structured call script while adapting naturally to real, sometimes difficult, patient conversations. • Strong active listening, empathy, and de-escalation skills; able to stay calm with anxious, confused, or distrustful patients. • Basic computer literacy and the ability to navigate a documentation platform (Mozaiq Care+) while talking with a patient. • Reliable high-speed internet, a quiet distraction-free workspace, and equipment suitable for handling sensitive health information. • Available to work scheduled shifts within the role’s Eastern Time (ET) operating window, including rotating evening or Saturday shifts. • Able to pass a background check and complete HIPAA / PHI-handling training prior to taking live patient calls. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS • Prior experience in a healthcare, medical office, insurance, or care-management call-center environment. • Familiarity with EHR, scheduling, or care-management platforms. • Experience working U.S. healthcare accounts or supporting U.S.-based patients. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE • Appointment-booked rate — the primary metric: every safe, reachable call ends in a scheduled PCP, specialist, or telehealth visit, or a documented same-day safety action. • Average Manager QA Scorecard score (100-point rubric covering opening/trust, privacy, safety screen, pathway accuracy, barrier resolution, conversion close, documentation, and role boundaries). • Zero automatic-fail incidents: no medication advice given, no false reassurance, no missed red-flag symptom, no unauthorized PHI disclosure. • Documentation completeness and accuracy in Mozaiq Care+ on every call. WHAT COLURE HEALTH OFFERS • Full paid training on the Care Continuity Outreach Playbook, safety-escalation protocols, and the Mozaiq Care+ platform before taking live calls. • Remote, work-from-home role with a defined, consistent shift schedule. • Ongoing call coaching and QA feedback from a dedicated supervisor. • Career growth path within Colure Health’s care-management organization, including pathways into Enrollment Specialist and senior coordinator roles. ROLE BOUNDARIES & COMPLIANCE Care Coordinators are not clinicians. Care Coordinators do not diagnose, clear symptoms, give medication advice, or tell a patient they are “fine.” Their job is to screen for safety, remove barriers, and get the patient to the right appointment or escalation — every call ends with a documented next step. title: Medical Scribe / Documentation QA (EHR Quality)
description: About Us We’re building a global talent pool of exceptional remote Medical Scribes / Documentation QA Specialists to support partner clinics across Australia, the US, the UK, New Zealand, and beyond. These clinics deliver modern healthcare through telehealth and digital services—often combining general practice with wellness, integrative care, and allied health support. Our shared mission is simple: make healthcare more human—by supporting clinicians with accurate, consistent documentation so patients receive safe, continuous care and clinics can operate with confidence. If you’re detail-oriented, privacy-minded, and love creating clean, clinician-ready charts, we’d love to meet you. Role Overview As a Medical Scribe / Documentation QA (EHR Quality), you’ll help ensure patient charts are complete, accurate, and easy for clinicians to use. Depending on clinic assignment, your work may include real-time or near-real-time scribing during telehealth visits, post-visit documentation cleanup, and ongoing chart audits to maintain consistent standards. This is a pooling/talent pipeline role. Successful candidates may be matched to open roles with clinics based on: • Your scribing and documentation experience (telehealth, in-person, specialty exposure) • Your preferred shift coverage (AU/UK/US) • EHR systems you’ve used (or your ability to learn quickly) • Compensation alignment and expected workload volume Note: You do not provide medical advice. Position Overview: United Chronic Care Management (UCCM) is seeking a compassionate, patient-focused, and highly organized Patient Navigation Specialist to help patients transform assessment findings into clear, actionable plans that support their health and wellness goals. This role serves as a critical bridge between assessment and action. After patients complete their health assessments, the Patient Care Plan Specialist works closely with them to identify priorities, establish meaningful goals, develop individualized care plans, and create a personalized "My Plan" that outlines the steps, services, and resources needed to achieve desired outcomes. The ideal candidate is an excellent communicator who is skilled at coaching, active listening, and patient engagement. This individual must be able to guide patients through goal-setting conversations, help them understand their care options, and develop practical action plans that align with their needs, preferences, and circumstances. This role is not simply documenting patient information—it is helping patients create a roadmap for success by turning assessment results into achievable goals, structured care plans, and coordinated next steps. Core Mission of the Role: To empower patients to take an active role in their health by developing personalized goals, creating comprehensive care plans, and guiding them through the next steps necessary to improve their health outcomes and overall well-being. Primary Responsibilities: - Care Plan Development Develop individualized care plans based on assessment findings and patient goals. Identify appropriate interventions, services, and support strategies to address patient needs. Ensure care plans are practical, achievable, and aligned with the patient's priorities. Regularly review and update care plans as patient needs and goals evolve. - Goal Setting Facilitate collaborative goal-setting conversations with patients. Help patients establish realistic, measurable, and meaningful short-term and long-term health goals. Assist patients in prioritizing goals based on their needs, readiness, and circumstances. Encourage accountability and patient ownership of their health journey. - My Plan Creation & Action Planning Create personalized "My Plan" documents that serve as a roadmap for each patient. Clearly outline patient goals, action steps, recommended services, follow-up activities, and expected outcomes. Educate patients on their care plans and ensure they understand their next steps. Help patients navigate and coordinate the services necessary to support their goals. - Documentation & Compliance Accurately document assessments, care plans, patient goals, progress notes, and follow-up activities. Maintain HIPAA compliance and patient confidentiality. Follow organizational policies, procedures, and quality standards. Contribute to continuous improvement efforts focused on patient engagement and outcomes. Desired Qualifications: Experience in healthcare, care coordination, patient navigation, health coaching, case management, or a related field. Strong communication, coaching, and motivational interviewing skills. Ability to build rapport and engage patients from diverse backgrounds. Strong organizational and documentation skills. Ability to develop structured care plans and action-oriented patient goals. Success in This Role Looks Like: Patients have clearly defined and measurable health goals. Personalized "My Plan" documents are completed accurately and on time. Care plans are actionable, patient-centered, and regularly updated. Patients understand their next steps and remain engaged in their care journey. Improved patient participation, adherence, and progress toward desired outcomes. Work Schedule Work hours are aligned with U.S. Eastern Time business operations. Specific shifts will be assigned during onboarding. Qualified applicants will be contacted for the next steps in the selection process.

description: Remote Medical Assistant – CCM, RPM & BHI Patient Support We are seeking a reliable, compassionate, and detail-oriented Remote Medical Assistant to join our team. This role involves working closely with patients enrolled in Chronic Care Management (CCM), Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM), and Behavioral Health Integration (BHI) programs. The ideal candidate is professional, dependable, comfortable speaking with patients over the phone, and able to document clearly and accurately. Position Responsibilities: Complete comprehensive monthly CCM calls with patients to review symptoms, medications, appointments, barriers to care, and overall health concerns. Support patients enrolled in RPM by reviewing vitals, clearing alerts, following up on abnormal readings, and encouraging patients to submit readings consistently. Assist with BHI outreach by checking in on patients’ emotional well-being, identifying concerns, and documenting patient-reported updates. Provide patient education, encouragement, and support while maintaining a warm and professional tone. Document all calls, interventions, alerts, and patient updates accurately in the system. Escalate urgent symptoms, abnormal trends, or patient concerns to the appropriate clinical team when needed. Maintain confidentiality and follow HIPAA guidelines at all times. What CCM, RPM, and BHI Mean: CCM — Chronic Care Management: Ongoing monthly support for patients with chronic conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, COPD, CHF, kidney disease, and other long-term health concerns. RPM — Remote Patient Monitoring: Monitoring patients’ home health readings such as blood pressure, blood sugar, weight, pulse, or oxygen levels and following up when readings are abnormal. BHI — Behavioral Health Integration: Supporting patients with mental health or emotional wellness needs by completing check-ins, identifying concerns, and helping connect them with appropriate care. Requirements: Medical Assistant experience preferred. Strong phone communication skills. Excellent documentation skills. Must be reliable, punctual, and able to work independently. Must be compassionate, patient-centered, and professional. Experience with CCM, RPM, BHI, EMR systems, or remote healthcare is a plus. Must be comfortable making outbound calls and speaking with patients daily. Pay: Pay is set at $3 USD biweekly/520 Monthly How to Apply: To be considered for this role, please send a video link introducing yourself and explaining: Why you are interested in this Remote Medical Assistant position. Your experience working with patients. Why you would be a great fit for CCM, RPM, and BHI support. How you demonstrate reliability, professionalism, and compassion in your work. We are looking for someone who truly cares about patient support, communicates well, and can be trusted to complete daily tasks with consistency and accuracy.
